results.title: California Memorial Stadium - University of California, Berkeley
results.snippet: Designed by John Galen Howard (although he had advised against the location, directly over the Hayward Fault and in the midst of a bird and wildlife sanctuary), the stadium opened in time for Cal to defeat Stanford there in the 1923 Big Game. It is a tribute to students killed in World War I.

results.title: California Memorial Stadium — Grokipedia
results.snippet: California Memorial Stadium opened and was dedicated on November 24, 1923, in conjunction with the University of California's football game against Stanford University, known as the Big Game. The venue was established as a memorial to Californians who died during World War I, with particular emphasis on University of California, Berkeley students, alumni, and residents who served and perished in the conflict.[11][1] Funding for the project came entirely from public contributions, reflecting widespread community support for honoring the war dead through a permanent athletic facility.[1] The dedication event doubled as the stadium's inaugural game, attracting an estimated 72,000 spectators—the largest crowd in its early history.
